latest_release.name: MyGo 0.9.2
latest_release.body:
## Changes in behavior

No breaking changes to the Go API. A few changes apps and builds may notice:

- **A launch waits for an instance that is shutting down.** With `RequestSingleInstanceLock`, the running instance now holds the lock until its process exits, so a `Relaunch`, an update's relaunch or a quick reopen waits for the old process to finish instead of running beside it. Two launches a few milliseconds apart no longer both run. (#1909, reported by @lizhongyue248 in #1906, with @yudongyouqing)
- **Notarized builds submit twice.** With `macos.notarize`, `mygo build` notarizes and staples the app before it goes into the disk image, then the image as before, which adds a few minutes. The app users drag to `/Applications` now passes Gatekeeper offline. (#1898, @PythonShe)

## Highlights

- **Every finger on a touchscreen.** `Element.Touches()` returns each finger that is down on an element, with an ID that lasts from landing to lifting, where it landed, its phase and its pressure, so a whiteboard on a large touchscreen can recognize its own gestures, such as a four-finger swipe to turn the page or a five-finger tap to clear it. `Touch.Width` and `Height` give the size of each contact, so the same whiteboard can erase with a palm and draw with a finger. Works on Windows and in browsers; Linux reports fingers but no contact size. The `Tester` gets `TouchDown`, `TouchMove`, `TouchUp` and `TouchCancel`. Apps that never call `Touches` don't link any of it. (#1884, #1907, requested by @chenxiao1990 in #1879)
- **Menus that stay open, with colored badges, on macOS.** `MenuItem.KeepOpen` keeps a menu open when one of its items is chosen, so a menu bar proxy app can let the user try nodes one after another, or start a latency test, without the submenu closing each time. `BadgeShape`, `BadgeColor` and `BadgeTextColor` draw a badge on a square, rounded or pill background, so latencies can be colored by how good they are, and the setters update them in place. Other platforms show the items and badges as before. (#741, #1913, @Sakurasan)
- **Cancel a call from the page.** A bound Go method can be called with an `AbortSignal`, as `fetch` is: `await Notes.add.with({ signal })("Groceries")`. Aborting rejects the promise right away and cancels the method's `context.Context`, so a search the user typed past or a long command they stopped ends in Go too. `AbortSignal.timeout` works as a time limit, and existing calls are unchanged. (#1781, @joei4cm, requested by @echoVic in #1759)

## New

### Native UI
- `ListState.MoveAnimation` makes rows glide to their places when rows above or around them come, go or move, such as a deleted item or a commit list rewritten by a reset, instead of jumping there in one frame. It respects reduced motion. (#1904, @PythonShe)
- `Element.PopoverMenu` takes `PopoverMenuOptions` with `Panel` and `Item`, as `PopoverMenuButton` does, so right-click menus can open with the same panel style and animation as the app's ⋯ menus. (#1889, requested by @tsugumi42 in #1885)
- A translucent web view over a transparent window fades with its element, such as a peek flyout's page fading in over a window left live behind it. (#1793, @joei4cm, requested by @ourongxing in #1026)

### The app
- `NowPlayingInfo.Artists` names each artist of a track. On Linux, media controls list them one by one; macOS, Windows and browsers show them joined. On Linux, the media controls can also bring the player's window to the front. (#1924, requested by @Shizuku11451 in #1923)
- On macOS, `TrayOptions.MonospacedTitle` keeps a tray title of a fixed number of characters at one width, so a network speed such as `↓999M ↑999M` doesn't shift the icons beside it as its units change. (#1882, @pseudoyu)

## Fixes

### Windows
- An app whose process an input method kept alive at exit, such as with Doubao IME, now exits, so a `Relaunch` can replace its executable. (#1897, reported by @mistquay in #1896)
- Iframes from another host of a custom scheme load thei

hot_issues.title: Layout performance: where mygo's flexbox loses time on arewelayoutyet's workloads
Touchscreen support: one-finger drag should scroll (Windows / Linux)
ui: each Tester's text system is never freed (one thread and font map per Tester since v0.9.1)
richtext: attachments that are elements (block embeds), as ui/editor's replacements
ui: Testers can't run in parallel — they share the glyph atlas
editor: hide or replace ranges, elements between lines, and per-line text styles (Markdown live preview)
Long rich text in virtualized lists: selection is lost when rows are recycled, and a long Markdown reply is built whole
Checkbox and Radio line up their box's bottom, not their label, in a Baseline row

detail.readme:
**Desktop apps in Go, with native UI or a web frontend.** Sponsored by:

Become a sponsor

--- Each MyGo window shows one of two kinds of interface, and one app, or one window, can mix them: - **A web page**, in the webview the OS already has: WKWebView on macOS, WebKitGTK on Linux, WebView2 on Windows. Build the frontend with any web tools; it calls your Go code through a TypeScript client generated from it. - **Native UI**, written in Go alone with package `ui` and drawn by MyGo itself on the GPU: no HTML, no JavaScript and no webview, so the window opens at once and takes little memory. Either way, an app is a single Go binary of a few megabytes, focused on low memory and CPU use. - **Pure Go, no cgo**: build for every platform from any machine. - **Typed IPC** for pages: bind Go services, stream values through channels and send typed events; the TypeScript client is generated from your Go code. - **A Go UI toolkit** for native UI: flexbox and grid layout, widgets, text editing with input methods, virtualized lists, SVG icons, animations, screen reader support, and views you test without a window; Liquid Glass on every platform with the glass plugin; web pages inside native UI, under the menus and dialogs it shows over them. - **Desktop APIs** for both: windows, menus, tray, dialogs, notifications, global shortcuts, deep links, file associations, recent documents, Now Playing and the media keys, the system accent color and accessibility settings, watching files, and more. - **Ready to ship**: app bundles and disk images, Windows installers, Debian and RPM packages, PKGBUILDs for Arch Linux and a Linux install script, code signing, notarization, and signed auto-updates with delta updates and an update window in the manner of Sparkle. A window with a web page, whose frontend calls Go: ```go type Greeter struct{} // Greet returns a greeting. func (Greeter) Greet(name string) string { return "Hello, " + name } func main() { mygo.Bind(Greeter{}) mygo.App.WhenReady(func() { mygo.NewWindow(mygo.WindowOptions{Title: "Hello", URL: "/"}) }) if err := mygo.App.Run(); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } } ``` ```ts import { Greeter } from "./mygo"; // generated document.body.textContent = await Greeter.greet("Ada"); ``` A window with native UI, whose view is a Go function of the app's state: ```go type counter struct{ n int } func (s *counter) view(c *ui.Context) { ui.Column(c).Fill().Center().Gap(12).Children(func() { ui.Text(c, fmt.Sprint(s.n)).FontSize(40).Bold() if ui.PrimaryButton(c, "Increment").Clicked() { s.n++ } }) } func main() { s := &counter{} mygo.App.WhenReady(func() { mygo.NewWindow(mygo.WindowOptions{ Title: "Counter", Content: ui.View(s.view), }) }) if err := mygo.App.Run(); err != nil { log.Fatal(err) } } ``` ## Getting started With [Go](https://go.dev/dl/) 1.27.3+ and [Bun](https://bun.sh), create an app with a web frontend: ```sh bunx mygo-cli init my-app # or: npx mygo-cli init my-app cd my-app bun run dev ``` An app of native UI needs Go alone: ```sh go run github.com/egoist/mygo/cmd/mygo@latest init -template native my-app cd my-app go tool mygo dev ``` Read the [documentation](docs/README.md). ## License MIT
